hits.name: Benjamin Bikman
hits.text:
A standard cholesterol panel can reveal insulin resistance, but you need to look at the markers that matter.

When people get their lipid results back, the attention almost always goes straight to LDL cholesterol. Despite decades of obsession over that number, LDL is a poor predictor of who will actually develop heart disease, and plenty of people who have heart attacks have LDL levels considered normal. The far more revealing pattern sits in two other lines on the same report, triglycerides and HDL.

Fasting triglycerides and the ratio of triglycerides to HDL are among the best simple markers of insulin resistance, alongside fasting insulin. A triglyceride level of about 130 mg/dL or higher, or a triglyceride-to-HDL ratio of about 3 or higher, flags insulin resistance about as well as the full set of metabolic syndrome criteria.

The biology behind this is straightforward. When the liver becomes insulin resistant and insulin stays high, the liver makes more fat and sends more of it into the blood as triglyceride-rich particles. As those particles are processed, HDL tends to fall and LDL particles become smaller and denser. High triglycerides and low HDL tend to show up together, and both stem from insulin resistance.

This is why two people can have the same LDL cholesterol and very different risk. The person with high triglycerides and low HDL is more likely to be carrying insulin resistance, which drives heart disease and type 2 diabetes far more than LDL ever has.

If a person wants a real read on their metabolic and heart health from a test they've probably already had, it's worth dividing triglycerides by HDL and paying far more attention to that number than to LDL.
hits.draft_en:
Ben Bikman says the most useful part of your cholesterol test isn't the LDL line.

Look at triglycerides and HDL. Divide triglycerides by HDL. He says a ratio of about 3 or more (in US mg/dL units), or triglycerides about 130 or higher, flags insulin resistance about as well as the full metabolic syndrome checklist.

Two blokes can have the same LDL and very different risk.

Over 50? Next time you get bloods back, ask your GP about your triglycerides and HDL, not just the LDL.

Insulin resistance contributes to certain cancers. Men with the most insulin resistance have nearly three times the odds of prostate cancer as men with the least.

Prostate cancer is one of the most common cancers in men. The conventional perspective is that it's caused by age, family history and sex hormones. Those matter, but insulin deserves a place on that list as well.

In one large study, the men in the top third for insulin resistance had nearly three times the odds of prostate cancer compared with the men in the bottom third. The most insulin-sensitive men had about a third of the odds. Men who had both the most insulin resistance and the most fat around the waist had the highest risk of all (8X higher than normal). 

While we often only see insulin through the lens of how it regulates glucose, insulin is a growth signal. It tells cells to take in fuel and use that fuel to build and divide. Cancer cells are no exception. In fact, many cancer cells carry more insulin receptors than normal cells, which equips them to be even more responsive to insulin's growth signals. 

If you're hoping to lower the risk of cancers tied to metabolism, keeping insulin low and insulin sensitivity high is worth the effort. It's also one of the few variables you can control.

virals.text:
We’re introducing Shirudo, an open-source Linux runtime allowing agents to defend systems without downtime. It lets agents write dynamic eBPF controls to shield systems from exploits, giving defenders more time to test and roll out patches. Built by @cisco together with OpenAI.

Shirudo is a first step toward self-defending infrastructure that can adapt to new threats while keeping services running. Our goal is for defenders to work with AI agents to find affected systems, test and share shields, and deploy them without disrupting workloads.

https://t.co/0AqGmcbxWH

Introducing OpenWorks, our program to fund local AI experts to help small businesses grow their business with AI.

AI is accelerating small business, lowering the barriers to entry (I've been increasingly hearing from people who left their job to start a small business because they have AI tools to support them) and helping them earn more.

virals.name: Satya Nadella
virals.text:
Outcome per dollar is the frontier. We’re advancing it at every layer: FLOPs-efficient pretraining (MAI Base 2), long RL climbs (Rocket), and token-efficient models (seven new MAI models announced last week). All driving better economics for our customers.

By building models and products together, we can keep hill-climbing and building models that deliver real-world tasks and passing the gains directly to customers, while staying open to every frontier model.
